borgwarner-haldex-gen4.name: BorgWarner Haldex Gen4 AWD controller (VAG PQ, 0AY 907 554)
borgwarner-haldex-gen4.notes: Mirror of what opentune-haldex implements for Gen4, as data: the read-only KWP2000/TP2.0 channel, the measuring-group cells it labels and the PQ drivetrain frames it decodes (a parity test in opentune-haldex keeps this file and the decoder in step). The ecudef holds the identify keys and the empty flash layout; no flash layout, MCU or checksum is publicly known. See docs/HALDEX.md.
safety: Changing the AWD lock changes how the car drives. Only act with the car stationary or in a safe place, and know how to return to stock behaviour.
OpenTune never writes to the Haldex controller itself (no coding, adaptation, basic settings, code clearing or flashing).
Bench work: follow the pinout and bench-safety notes of the database unit, and check the pinout on your own unit first.

mercedes-egs5x-7226.name: Mercedes 722.6 5-speed automatic (NAG1) - EGS / EGS51 TCU
mercedes-egs5x-7226.notes: External (body-mounted) TCU of the 722.6 five-speed automatic. One CAN generation is defined: 'egs51' (pre-2000 EGS/EGS51 cars, 500 kbit/s), transcribed from the Ultimate-NAG52 project's hand-made EGS51 matrix. The frame layout of the later EGS52 (CAN-C, 2000+) cars is deliberately NOT included: it will be re-derived from a listen-only capture of the owner's own car. A W210 can be either generation; docs/MERCEDES-722.6.md describes how to tell them apart from a capture (by CAN ids, and by the gear coding in 0x218, which on EGS51 is R = 6 / P = 8). Everything here is passive CAN decode plus documentation: OpenTune does not transmit to this TCU, read its flash or know its checksum. Diagnostics: pre-2000 units are diagnosed on the K-line (C1 pin 1, see the database unit) with a protocol the cited sources do not document, so no diagnostic channel is declared. Tables describe the calibration structure of the open Ultimate-NAG52 replacement firmware (shift schedules, shift time, fill, TCC and adaptation maps), not the stock EGS flash layout, which is not publicly documented; no values are shipped. Validation: synthetic CAN frames built from the published layout only - nothing has been checked against a capture from a real car yet.
safety: The 722.6 TCU sets line, shift and lock-up pressures: wrong maps or adaptations can slip and burn clutches or wreck the gearbox, and a gearbox fault can make the car move unexpectedly or lose drive in traffic.

OpenTune only listens here: it never transmits on the powertrain CAN for this unit. Do not replay captured frames onto a running car - GS_218 carries the TCU's engine-torque request and the engine acts on it.
Capture with a listen-only adapter where possible, car stationary or on a safe road, and never wire into CAN-C while the engine runs.
The tables describe the Ultimate-NAG52 replacement firmware; do not assume the stock EGS51/52 stores the same tables or values.

openhaldex-c6.name: OpenHaldex controller (open-source Haldex lock-request box)
openhaldex-c6.notes: Aftermarket box that sits between the car and the Haldex and rewrites the lock request. Its CAN broadcast/command frames and supplier UDS DIDs as opentune-haldex implements them (parity-tested). The mode write is done by `opentune haldex mode set` (confirm-gated, read back).
safety: Changing the AWD lock changes how the car drives. Only act with the car stationary or in a safe place, and know how to return to stock behaviour.
Mode changes are writes: they need --confirm and are read back; a disabled controller ignores them.

vag-dq250-02e.name: VAG DQ250 6-speed DSG (02E, PQ35/PQ46) - Temic TCU J743
vag-dq250-02e.notes: Controller view of the 02E mechatronic. Flash layout, maps and checksum live in the two ecudefs (one per software generation): temic-dq250-02e (PowerPC, dq250-02e checksum real-image-tested 78/78, 30 shift tables MEDIUM) and temic-dq250-02e-tricore (no checksum). Diagnostics: neither channel is confirmed for 02E; PQ-era workshop diagnostics commonly run KWP2000 over VW TP2.0. live[] is intentionally empty: the meaning of each 02E measuring group is parked until a real capture exists; add kwp_measuring_block entries here from a capture and `opentune dsg groups` labels those cells (all others read as unconfirmed). See docs/DSG.md.
safety: A DSG TCU controls clutch pressure. Wrong shift or clutch data can damage the clutches or the gearbox and can make a car move unexpectedly. Edit by ratio, keep downshift points below their upshift points, and keep a verified stock read.
Only calibration editing is in scope: no launch-control, torque-limiter or protection defeat.
Bench reads: current-limited supply, fused +12 V, CAN terminated (see the database unit).

flash.notes: AL551 (method 0x22) image offsets from the zf8hp checksum handler: CRC-32 over 0x190000..=0x1FFD5F, stored at 0x180244. AES variants and Gen3 TriCore are not covered.

zf-8hp-gen1.name: ZF 8HP first-generation TCU (8HP45/55/70/90)
zf-8hp-gen1.notes: Drop-in example of a non-VAG controller: identity, the zf8hp CAL checksum (AL551 generation, CRC-32 vectors + synthetic only) and the first-generation gear ratios. The CAL_DATA region is the one the zf8hp checksum covers in an AL551 image; the full image size and other regions are not claimed. Diagnostics differ per brand (BMW, Audi, FCA) and are not declared until a cited source documents them.
safety: An 8HP TCU controls clutch pressures: wrong calibration data can destroy clutches or make the car move unexpectedly.
The 8HP TCU has no internal CAN termination; on the bench fit 120 ohm at the TCU and apply the main supply before wake-up (database unit).
